## Employee
- Name: Gandu (no id)
- Role: Instrumentation Engineer, Instrumentation
- Plant / unit: Haldia  / Unit 300

## Equipment history in the knowledge graph
- none found for this profile; interview from the profile alone and ask them to name their key equipment

topics.title: Role evolution and unwritten responsibilities
topics.rationale: No equipment records exist for this profile; understanding what the engineer actually did day-to-day is the foundation.
seed_questions: What were the top three things you were responsible for that never appeared in any official job description?
Which tasks did you inherit informally from previous engineers that were never formally handed over?
What part of your role will be hardest to explain to your successor?

topics.title: Key instrumentation assets in Unit 300
topics.rationale: No equipment is linked to this profile; the engineer must name the critical instruments they owned.
seed_questions: Which specific transmitters, valves, or analysers in Unit 300 have demanded the most of your attention over the years?
If you had to pick the three most troublesome instrument tags in the unit, what would they be?
Are there any instruments that are critical to safety or production but are poorly documented?

topics.title: Chronic instrument failure patterns
topics.rationale: Undocumented failure modes and the real reasons behind repeat failures are high-value knowledge at risk of loss.
seed_questions: Which instruments have failed repeatedly despite being 'fixed' each time, and what do you believe the real root cause is?
Are there any instruments where the installed material or specification is wrong for the process conditions, but it was never formally changed?
What early-warning signs do you look for that indicate an instrument is about to fail, that aren't in any manual?

topics.title: Undocumented calibration and tuning values
topics.rationale: Engineers often carry controller tuning parameters, calibration offsets, and range settings in their heads or personal notebooks.
seed_questions: Are there any controller tuning parameters or calibration offsets you've settled on over time that differ from the official datasheets?
Which loops have you deliberately detuned or run in manual to work around a problem that was never fully resolved?
Do you have personal notes or a 'black book' of settings that your successor will need?

topics.title: Vendor and service provider quirks
topics.rationale: Knowing which vendor contacts are helpful, which parts have long lead times, and which service providers to avoid is critical tribal knowledge.
seed_questions: Which vendor technical contacts have been invaluable to you, and what's the best way to reach them?
Are there any instruments where the OEM no longer supports the model, and you've had to find creative workarounds?
Which local service providers or contractors do you trust for instrumentation work, and which ones should your successor be cautious about?

topics.title: Unit 300 shutdown and turnaround instrumentation scope
topics.rationale: Shutdowns and turnarounds have critical instrument tasks that are often in the engineer's head, not in the work order system.
seed_questions: What instrumentation tasks do you always include in a shutdown that never seem to make it onto the official planning list?
Are there any instruments that can only be accessed or maintained during a shutdown, and what is the exact sequence of work?
What went wrong during the last turnaround that your successor should watch out for?

topics.title: Interlock bypasses and safety system workarounds
topics.rationale: Temporary bypasses that became permanent, or known weaknesses in the safety instrumented system, are high-risk undocumented items.
seed_questions: Are there any interlock bypasses or force-enables currently in place that have been there longer than anyone would like to admit?
Which safety instrumented functions have you had the least confidence in, and why?
What is the one thing in the safety system that keeps you up at night?

topics.title: Half-finished instrumentation projects and modifications
topics.rationale: Projects that were started but not completed, or modifications that were partially implemented, represent significant risk.
seed_questions: Which instrumentation upgrade or migration projects did you start but never get to finish?
Are there any partially installed instruments or wiring that are sitting disconnected, and what was the original plan?
What modification requests or improvement ideas did you submit that were approved but never executed?

topics.title: Process and operations interface pain points
topics.rationale: The relationship between instrumentation and operations often involves unwritten agreements, workarounds, and communication norms.
seed_questions: Which operators have the best instinct for when an instrument reading is wrong, and how do they communicate that to you?
Are there any recurring disagreements between operations and instrumentation about whether a reading is real or a fault?
What is the unwritten protocol for escalating an instrument problem in the middle of the night?

topics.title: Spare parts and obsolescence risks
topics.rationale: Knowledge of which spares are critical, which are obsolete, and where substitutes can be found is often entirely in the engineer's head.
seed_questions: Which critical spares are you down to your last unit of, and what is the plan when it's gone?
Are there any instruments where you've found a compatible substitute part that isn't in the official BOM?
What obsolete instrument models in Unit 300 are you most worried about, and have you identified any migration paths?

topics.title: Documentation gaps and tribal knowledge sources
topics.rationale: Knowing which drawings are wrong, which manuals are missing, and who else holds critical knowledge is essential for the successor.
seed_questions: Which P&IDs, loop drawings, or wiring diagrams for Unit 300 do you know contain errors, and what are the corrections?
Who else in the plant (operators, other engineers, technicians) holds critical instrumentation knowledge that isn't written down anywhere?
If your successor could only read three documents to understand the instrumentation in Unit 300, what would they be—and what would still be missing?

topics.title: Successor advice and open risks
topics.rationale: A direct handover topic ensures the retiring engineer can give unfiltered advice to their successor and flag the biggest open risks.
seed_questions: What is the single most important piece of advice you would give your successor on their first day?
What is the one problem you believe is most likely to cause a serious incident after you leave if it isn't addressed?
If you had 30 more days before retirement, what would you spend them doing?
